verses.1:1: Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith of equal preciousness with ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
verses.1:2: May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the full knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: Seeing that His divine power has bestowed upon us all things pertaining to life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and virtue,
verses.1:4: through which He has given to us His precious and greatest promises, that by these you may become sharers in the divine nature, having fled the corruption that is in the world through evil desire.
verses.1:5: And for this very reason, applying all diligence, in your faith supply virtue, and in virtue knowledge,
verses.1:6: and in knowledge self-control, and in self-control steadfastness, and in steadfastness godliness,
verses.1:7: and in godliness brotherly kindness, and in brotherly kindness love.
verses.1:8: For if these things are yours and are abounding, they render you neither idle nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: For whoever lacks these things is blind, being shortsighted, and has forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.
verses.1:10: Therefore, brethren, be all the more diligent to confirm your calling and election; for if you do these things, you shall never stumble;
verses.1:11: for in this manner the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
verses.1:12: Therefore I intend always to remind you concerning these things, even though you know them and are firmly established in the present truth.
verses.1:13: And I consider it right, as long as I remain in this tabernacle, to stir you up by reminder,
verses.1:14: knowing that the putting off of my tabernacle is soon, just as our Lord Jesus Christ also showed me.
verses.1:15: And I will also be diligent that after my departure you may be able at all times to call these things to remembrance.
verses.1:16: For we did not follow artfully devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we had become eyewitnesses of His majesty.
verses.1:17: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when such a voice was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory, "This is My Son, My beloved, in whom I am well pleased"—
verses.1:18: and this voice we ourselves heard borne out of heaven while we were with Him on the holy mountain.
verses.1:19: And we have the prophetic word made more certain, to which you do well to give heed as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts;
verses.1:20: knowing this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation;
verses.1:21: for no prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were borne along by the Holy Spirit.
verses.2:1: Yet false prophets also rose up among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who will covertly bring in ruinous heresies, even denying the Master who purchased them, drawing upon themselves swift destruction.
verses.2:2: And many will follow their licentious ways, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed;
verses.2:3: and in covetousness they will exploit you with fabricated words; for them the judgment from long ago is not idle, and their destruction does not slumber.
verses.2:4: For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and delivered them to pits of gloom to be kept for judgment,
verses.2:5: and did not spare the world of old, but guarded Noah, a proclaimer of righteousness, together with seven others, when He brought a deluge upon a world of the ungodly;
verses.2:6: and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, condemned them to utter overthrow, setting them forth as an example to those who would afterward live in ungodliness;
verses.2:7: and rescued righteous Lot, who was greatly distressed by the licentious conduct of the lawless—
verses.2:8: for by what he saw and heard, that righteous man, dwelling among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day because of their lawless deeds—
verses.2:9: then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly out of trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment,
verses.2:10: and especially those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they do not tremble to revile the glorious ones,
verses.2:11: whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against them before the Lord.
verses.2:12: But these men, like unreasoning beasts born by instinct to be captured and destroyed, reviling matters of which they are ignorant, shall also be destroyed in their own destruction,
verses.2:13: suffering harm as the wages of unrighteousness. They count it pleasure to indulge in revelry in the daytime; they are spots and blemishes, reveling in their own deceptions while they feast with you,
verses.2:14: having eyes full of adultery and that never cease from sin, enticing unstable souls, having a heart trained in covetousness—children of a curse!
verses.2:15: Forsaking the straight way, they have gone astray, having followed the way of Balaam, the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness,
verses.2:16: but he received a rebuke for his own transgression: a speechless donkey, speaking with a human voice, restrained the madness of the prophet.
verses.2:17: These are waterless springs and mists driven by a tempest, for whom the gloom of darkness has been reserved.
verses.2:18: For speaking arrogant words of vanity, they entice through the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are barely escaping from those who walk in error,
verses.2:19: promising them liberty, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whatever a man is overcome, to that he is enslaved.
verses.2:20: For if, after having escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse than the first.
verses.2:21: For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after knowing it to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.
verses.2:22: What the true proverb says has happened to them: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in the mire."
verses.3:1: Beloved, this is now the second epistle I am writing to you, in both of which I am stirring up your sincere mind by reminder,
verses.3:2: that you should remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Savior given through your apostles,
verses.3:3: knowing this first of all, that in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, walking according to their own lusts,
verses.3:4: and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue just as they have been from the beginning of creation."
verses.3:5: For they willfully overlook this fact, that by the word of God the heavens existed from long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water,
verses.3:6: by which the world that then existed perished, being deluged with water.
verses.3:7: But the heavens and the earth that now exist have been stored up by the same word for fire, being kept until the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
verses.3:8: But do not let this one thing escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
verses.3:9: The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some regard slowness, but is longsuffering toward you, not desiring that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
verses.3:10: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a mighty roar, and the elements will be dissolved in fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are in it will be laid bare.
verses.3:11: Since all these things are thus to be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness,
verses.3:12: looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be set ablaze and dissolved, and the elements will melt away in fervent heat?
verses.3:13: Yet according to His promise we await new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
verses.3:14: Therefore, beloved, since you await these things, be diligent to be found by Him in peace, without spot and blameless;
verses.3:15: and consider the longsuffering of our Lord to be salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
verses.3:16: as he also does in all his epistles, speaking in them concerning these things; in which there are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable distort, as they also do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
verses.3:17: You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard, lest being led away with the error of the lawless, you fall from your own steadfastness;
verses.3:18: but grow in grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

notes.1:1: The Greek text uses Simeon (Symeon), the Semitic form of Simon. The phrase "our God and Savior Jesus Christ" shares a single Greek article, identifying Jesus Christ as both God and Savior.
notes.1:3: Early manuscripts read "by His own glory and virtue" (or "excellence"), whereas later manuscripts read "to glory and virtue."
notes.1:12: Early manuscripts read "I intend" (or "I will always be ready"), whereas later manuscripts read "I will not be negligent."
notes.1:20: "From one's own interpretation" is debated as referring either to a reader's private interpretation or to a prophet's own human origination and unraveling of a vision, the latter connecting directly with verse twenty-one.
notes.2:4: The Greek verb rendered "cast them into Tartarus" occurs only here in the New Testament, denoting the lowest abyss of the underworld. Early manuscripts read "pits of gloom," whereas later manuscripts read "chains of darkness."
notes.2:13: Early manuscripts read "suffering harm" (creating a wordplay with "unrighteousness") and "deceptions," whereas other manuscripts read "receiving" and "love feasts."
notes.2:15: The Greek text gives the name Bosor, corresponding to Hebrew Beor in Numbers 22:5.
notes.2:18: Early manuscripts read "barely" (or "scarcely"), whereas later manuscripts read "actually" (or "truly").
notes.3:2: Early manuscripts read "your apostles," whereas later manuscripts read "us, the apostles."
notes.3:10: Early manuscripts read "will be found" (rendered "will be laid bare," signifying exposure to God's judgment), whereas later manuscripts read "will be burned up."
notes.3:12: "Hastening" may denote either earnestly longing for the day of God or hastening its arrival through godly living and repentance.
notes.3:18: "To the day of eternity" translates a unique New Testament phrase signifying the unending eternal day.
